asA: reviewer (with Codex) at the REVIEW stage
iWant: to record one verdict with a code axis and a test-adequacy axis, the touched criteria and each finding with its locus
soThat: Finalise and the next round read my verdict from the branch, not from a message
description: rcf build verdict review and ReviewVerdict v1.
title: A reviewer records the REVIEW verdict, code and test adequacy, at the reviewed head

acceptanceCriteria.description: [happy] Given a fixture project at a clean committed HEAD H whose FBS-001 scopes AC-101-1 and AC-101-2, when rcf build verdict review --fbs FBS-001 --acs AC-101-1,AC-101-2 --code MERGE --adequacy PASS --by "reviewer and codex" runs, then it exits 0, stdout is "verdict: review MERGE/PASS at <H7> written to rcf/verdicts/<H12>/review.json", and that file parses as ReviewVerdict v1 with head equal to the full sha of H, fbsIds ["FBS-001"], touchedAcIds ["AC-101-1", "AC-101-2"], findings [] and recordedBy "reviewer and codex"; no commit is made.

[happy] Given the same fixture, when rcf build verdict review --fbs FBS-001 --acs AC-101-1 --code MERGE --adequacy FINDINGS --finding "spec:AC-101-1:the then clause names no exit code" --finding "build:-:the CHANGELOG line is missing" runs, then it exits 0 and the file records adequacy "FINDINGS" with findings [{ id "F-1", locus "spec", acId "AC-101-1", text "the then clause names no exit code" }, { id "F-2", locus "build", acId null, text "the CHANGELOG line is missing" }].

[failure] Given the same fixture, when the verb runs with --code FINDINGS and no --finding it exits 2 with stderr "[error] usage FINDINGS needs at least one --finding"; with --finding "maybe:AC-101-1:x" it exits 2 naming the expected form <spec|build>:<AC id|->:<text>; with --acs AC-999-1 it exits 3 with stderr "[error] brokenReference AC-999-1 is not scoped by FBS-001"; and in each case no file appears under rcf/verdicts/.
acceptanceCriteria.supersessionNote: Retired 2026-10-26 (stage-keeper ruling RC-10, round A ruling 5: retired and succeeded, never reworded): --finding takes a test locus beside spec and build (AC-19701-7), so the expected form <spec|build>:<AC id|->:<text> no longer holds; TAC-4154 names <spec|build|test>.

acceptanceCriteria.description: [failure] Given an uncommitted change to src/x.js, the verb exits 4 with stderr "verdict refused: working tree is dirty; a verdict names a committed head"; given rcf/verdicts/<H12>/review.json already present, a second run exits 4 with stderr "verdict refused: a review verdict for <H7> already exists at rcf/verdicts/<H12>/review.json" and the existing file is byte-identical afterwards.

[must-not] rcf build verdict review never writes outside rcf/verdicts/<H12>/, never commits, never edits an existing verdict file and never spawns anything but git: after any run, git status --porcelain lists at most that one new file.

[failure] Given FBS-001 at inProgress scoping AC-101-1, AC-101-2 and AC-101-3, rcf build verdict review --fbs FBS-001 --acs AC-101-1,AC-101-2 --code MERGE --adequacy PASS exits 3 with stderr "[error] brokenReference touched criteria omit AC-101-3 of FBS-001 (inProgress)" and writes nothing; with FBS-001 at complete the same command writes the verdict (an amend round).

[happy] Given the same fixture, when rcf build verdict review --fbs FBS-001 --acs AC-101-1,AC-101-2 --code MERGE --adequacy FINDINGS --finding "test:AC-101-1:the bound test survives the noOp mutant" runs, then it exits 0 and the file records findings [{ id "F-1", locus "test", acId "AC-101-1", text "the bound test survives the noOp mutant" }]: --finding takes a test locus beside spec and build.
